question: In a certain code language, ‘STORK’ is written as ‘URROO’ and ‘ASHES’ is written as ‘CQKBW’. How will ‘BUNKE’ be written in that language?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The logic followed here is:

For, 'STORK’ is written as ‘URROO',

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9607ff9a352999f0ded486d5ab8f29831f035c4e62e8345fdd861d64979c15f.png] 

For, 'ASHES’ is written as ‘CQKBW',

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dc7615dc04df3de02b27fd1d5076080836f1aab07feb9f96e68d1b34f2ee84a.png] 

Similarly, for '**BUNKE**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52db03f03ec3d10c0b6471a68687baaf19586e0fd7ce0587ef31989de0f0b6fe.png] 

So, 'BUNKE' will be written as '**DSQHI**'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
